system.name: Themis
system.one_liner: a scheduling-aware buffer manager that lets a single hierarchical-bitmap queue structure efficiently manage a hybrid SRAM+HBM packet buffer in router chips

components.name: Traffic Manager
components.role: panel (a): the router-chip module containing buffer management, on caption Traffic Manager (TM)

components.name: Buffer Manager
components.role: admits each packet and decides whether it is stored in on-chip or off-chip memory

components.name: Scheduler
components.role: enqueues and later dequeues packets for departure

components.name: Buffer Read/Write Controller
components.role: stores packet data and descriptors on write, and reads out packets and releases buffer space on dequeue

components.name: Hybrid Buffer
components.role: combined on-chip/off-chip packet storage managed by the TM

components.name: On-Chip Buffer (e.g., SRAM)
components.role: fast on-chip packet storage

components.name: Off-Chip Buffer (e.g., DRAM)
components.role: larger off-chip packet storage

components.name: Statistics Module
components.role: tracks buffer occupancy/usage statistics

components.name: Ingress Packet Processing
components.role: pipeline stage feeding packets into the Buffer Manager

components.name: Egress Packet Processing
components.role: pipeline stage receiving packets read out of the buffer

components.name: PD Memory
components.role: panel (b): stores per-packet descriptors as a linked list with a Head pointer

components.name: Packet descriptor
components.role: metadata record for a buffered packet, chained into PD Memory's linked list

components.name: Cell Pointer Memory
components.role: holds linked cell-pointer lists per packet plus a free-cell pointer list

components.name: Free Cell Pointer List
components.role: linked list of unused cell pointers available for allocation

components.name: Cell Data Memory
components.role: fixed-size storage cells holding the actual packet data

components.name: L1
components.role: first-level counters/bitmap over the hybrid buffer used by the scheduler's FLS/FFS logic

components.name: L2
components.role: second-level counters/bitmap refining the L1 hierarchy

components.name: PB
components.role: priority buckets organized as a tree beneath the L1/L2 bitmap hierarchy

components.name: SRAM Free List
components.role: free-cell-pointer list for the SRAM portion of the hybrid buffer

components.name: HBM Free List
components.role: free-cell-pointer list for the HBM portion of the hybrid buffer

components.name: SRAM R/W Controller
components.role: reads/writes packets in SRAM and participates in swap-out/swap-in with HBM

components.name: HBM R/W Controller
components.role: reads/writes packets in HBM and participates in swap-out/swap-in with SRAM

components.name: SRAM
components.role: on-chip tier of Themis's hybrid buffer

components.name: HBM
components.role: off-chip high-bandwidth-memory tier of Themis's hybrid buffer

flows.what: incoming packet admitted; Buffer Manager decides on-chip vs off-chip storage
admitted packet forwarded to be written
Write In: packet data and descriptor stored
buffer read/write controller reads out the packet and releases the associated buffer space
a packet descriptor's cell pointer list identifies the cells holding its data
cell pointers reference the fixed-size cells storing packet data
hierarchical bitmap traversal locates the target priority bucket and updates path counters/bitmaps, storing the packet in SRAM
a unified centralized controller orchestrates swap-out (FLS) to HBM and swap-in (FFS) from HBM
FFS identifies the highest-priority non-empty bucket across SRAM and HBM and dequeues the corresponding packet

content.key_idea: A single hierarchical-bitmap priority-queue structure (bitmap trie over priority buckets, BBQ) can manage a hybrid SRAM+HBM packet buffer with minimal extra logic by adding a centralized controller that transparently swaps packets between SRAM and HBM using FLS/FFS bitmap operations.

summary: Figure 8 shows, in three panels, how Themis fits into a router chip's existing Traffic Manager. Panel (a) is the generic TM pipeline: a Buffer Manager admits packets and picks on-chip or off-chip storage, a Buffer Read/Write Controller stores packet data and descriptors, a Scheduler later dequeues packets, and the controller reads them out and frees buffer space, backed by a Hybrid Buffer (on-chip SRAM plus off-chip DRAM/HBM) and a Statistics Module. Panel (b) shows the buffer's memory layout: PD Memory holding linked packet descriptors, Cell Pointer Memory holding per-packet cell-pointer lists and a free list, and Cell Data Memory holding fixed-size data cells. Panel (c) is Themis itself: a hierarchical bitmap (L1/L2 counters, priority buckets PB) that locates buckets and stores packets in SRAM on enqueue, plus a centralized controller that swaps packets between SRAM and HBM (FLS/FFS) and, on dequeue, finds the highest-priority non-empty bucket across both tiers.

notes: layout-proposal: three-panel subsystem gallery — a linear TM pipeline (a), a linked-list buffer-pointer memory diagram (b), and a hierarchical bitmap/tree scheduler diagram (c) placed side by side under one Data-Path/Control-Path legend, not matching any single named template. The context text describes panels (a) and (c) in detail but has no paragraph for panel (b) (Buffer Architecture), whose components are read from figure labels only; the mapping of all eight circled step numbers in panel (a) to specific arrows is a best-effort reconstruction from the four macro-steps described in prose.
